**Repo root**: /home/ross/Dev/dev-tools
**Parity check**: `scripts/verify-shared-blocks.sh` (if executable) checks that `## Flow Context` and `## Ledger Schema` blocks remain byte-identical across review.md, review-apply.md, optimise.md, optimise-apply.md.
**Today's date**: 2026-04-18

## Output contract — CRITICAL

Tag each item with exactly ONE of:
- `applied R{n}: <summary>` — you wrote bytes for R{n}
- `applied R{n}: partial — <done>; skipped parts: <not done>` — partial
- `verified-clean R{n}: <audit note>` — already matches; wrote no bytes
- `skipped R{n}: <reason>` — cannot safely apply; wrote no bytes

**Hard rule**: no bytes written for R{n} → `verified-clean` or `skipped`, NEVER `applied`.

## Pre-analysed interface contracts (the Rust agent is committing to these shapes)

The Rust agent is adding two new flags that YOUR docs updates should reference:

- **R1**: `tomlctl items list --count` becomes real. Output is `{"count": N}` (JSON). Use this in doc examples that previously had `tomlctl items list <file> --count`.
- **R14**: `tomlctl items apply --array <name>` (default `"items"`) becomes real. Use this in docs for the rollback_events append: `printf '%s' "$EVENT_JSON" | tomlctl items apply <ledger> --array rollback_events --ops -`.

Reference these exact command shapes in your doc updates.

## Items

### R1 — doc updates for `tomlctl items list --count` (critical, completeness)
**Files**: `claude/commands/review.md:500`, `claude/commands/optimise.md:507`
**Fix**: both files already reference `tomlctl items list --count`. The Rust agent is adding the flag; your job is to verify the prose reads correctly once the flag exists, and — if the current text is just `tomlctl items list <ledger> --count` — update the example to consume it properly (e.g. `[ "$(tomlctl items list <ledger> --status open --count | jq -r .count)" = "0" ]` or similar). Do NOT change the flag name. ALSO propagate to `claude/skills/tomlctl/SKILL.md` (filter section around line 51-66) and `tomlctl/README.md` (around line 22) — these should document the `--count` flag alongside the other filters.

### R6 — sidecar doc clarity (trivial, security)
**Files**: `tomlctl/README.md` (~line 56-61), `claude/skills/tomlctl/SKILL.md` (~line 280-291)
**Fix**: add ONE sentence to each clarifying the threat model. Suggested wording (adapt to local tone):

> The sidecar is a consistency check against accidental corruption and collaborative out-of-band edits — it is **not** a MAC or tamper-proof signature. An attacker with ledger write access can trivially rewrite the sidecar; hostile-actor threat models still require auditing the ledger's git history.

`claude/commands/review-apply.md` line ~552 already says something similar; pattern-match its phrasing for consistency.

ALSO: as a concurrent pre-commit to the Rust agent's R3 (TOCTOU) work, downgrade the `.claude/` containment language in README.md (~line 313) and SKILL.md (~line 313) from a hard security guarantee to "best-effort guard against agent/user typos". Do NOT remove the guard description — just soften the claim from "refuses to touch files outside .claude/" to "best-effort containment guard, not a sandbox". Keep it concise.

### R8 — `/review` disposition stdin form (small, security)
**File**: `claude/commands/review.md` around line 628 (Step 4 — Handle Dispositions)
**Fix**: currently shows `tomlctl items update <ledger> R{n} --json '{"status":"deferred","defer_reason":"...","defer_trigger":"..."}'`. Replace with the stdin form shown in review-apply.md:584:

```bash
printf '%s' '{"status":"deferred","defer_reason":"...","defer_trigger":"..."}' | tomlctl items update <ledger> R{n} --json -
```

Explain briefly (one line) that the stdin form avoids shell-quoting issues when user-supplied `reason` / `trigger` / `rationale` contain `'`, `$`, `` ` ``, or newlines. Apply same fix pattern to the `wontfix` example just below.

Mirror the change to `claude/commands/optimise.md`'s equivalent disposition section if it exists.

### R10 — CLAUDE.md setup references untracked paths (trivial, completeness)
**File**: `CLAUDE.md` (root of repo, currently untracked per git status)
**Check first**: run `git status CLAUDE.md .githooks scripts 2>&1` — confirm `.githooks/` and `scripts/` are still untracked.

> This repository uses a repo-local git hooks directory at `.githooks/` for parity enforcement …

to a variant that notes the hook dir is created alongside the shared-block machinery and cross-references the files. Add a short sentence at the end of the setup section:

> **Note**: if `.githooks/` or `scripts/verify-shared-blocks.sh` are not yet present in your clone, the shared-block parity check will silently no-op until they land. Run `ls .githooks scripts` to confirm before relying on the hook.

This is a `applied R10: partial — soften CLAUDE.md; skipped parts: committing .githooks/ and scripts/ (requires separate commit)`.

### R11 — UK/US spelling drift (trivial, quality)
**Files**: `claude/commands/optimise.md`, `claude/commands/optimise-apply.md`
**Fix**: standardise on UK spelling throughout. Pattern replacements (case-sensitive, word-boundary):
- `behavior` → `behaviour`

- `optimize` → `optimise` (already partial — finish the pass)

Check the other two command files (`review.md`, `review-apply.md`) for any strays too — they should already be UK-consistent but audit.

**Exception**: if any file literally embeds code that names US spellings (unlikely here), preserve those. Only change prose.

### R12 — new SHARED-BLOCKs for apply-step-3-4-5.5 + apply-constraints (medium, quality)
**Files**: `claude/commands/review-apply.md`, `claude/commands/optimise-apply.md`, `scripts/shared-blocks.toml` (untracked — check if exists and present in working tree)
**Threat model / invariant**: drift between the two apply commands has historically caused duplicate-finding cycles (per CLAUDE.md). Current state: Step 3 / Step 4 / Step 5 / Step 5.5 / Important Constraints sections are ~90% byte-identical with only `R{n}` vs `O{n}`, `fix` vs `optimisation`, `review-apply` vs `optimise-apply` substitutions.

**The substitutions prevent byte-identical parity** — SHARED-BLOCK enforcement requires exact byte match. So you CANNOT simply wrap existing text in SHARED-BLOCK markers; that would fail `scripts/verify-shared-blocks.sh`.

**Pragmatic fix**: identify the largest contiguous byte-identical subsections (regions where neither `R` / `O` nor `fix` / `optimisation` appears — typically the general prose around dedup, secret-scans, constraint bullets that use generic language like "agent" / "ledger item"). Wrap ONLY those truly byte-identical subsections in a new SHARED-BLOCK:

```markdown
<!-- SHARED-BLOCK:apply-constraints START -->
...byte-identical prose...
<!-- SHARED-BLOCK:apply-constraints END -->
```

Add an entry to `scripts/shared-blocks.toml` for the new block. If the shared-blocks.toml manifest is untracked or absent, check if it lives somewhere else — grep the repo for `SHARED-BLOCK:flow-context` to find the manifest format, then add by pattern. If you cannot find or safely extend the manifest: `skipped R12: shared-blocks.toml manifest not found; propose extracting apply-constraints block in a follow-up when manifest location is confirmed`.

**Scope discipline**: the finding suggests BOTH an apply-rollback-protocol block AND an apply-constraints block. Pick ONE to extract this round (whichever has the largest byte-identical subsection); leave the other for a follow-up. Partial-apply with clear notes is preferred over overreach.

### R13 — parse vs get verb drift (trivial, quality)
**Files**: `claude/skills/tomlctl/SKILL.md` (~line 44, 47), `tomlctl/README.md` (~line 22), `claude/commands/review.md` (~line 360), `claude/commands/optimise.md` (~line 540)
**Threat model / invariant**: two equivalent CLI verbs (`tomlctl parse <file>` vs `tomlctl get <file>` with no path) creates doc drift. Goal: one canonical verb referenced consistently.

**Pick `tomlctl get <file>`** (no path argument) as canonical — it's the more general form (get with path = scalar read; get without path = whole doc). Update SKILL.md and any other doc that currently uses `tomlctl parse <file>` for whole-doc reads to use `tomlctl get <file>` instead. Leave the `parse` subcommand in the Rust code as an alias for backward compat (the Rust agent is NOT modifying this; `parse` stays callable, just deprecated-in-docs).

Specifically:
- SKILL.md line ~44, 47: change `tomlctl parse` → `tomlctl get`
- review.md line ~360: change `tomlctl --verify-integrity parse` → `tomlctl --verify-integrity get`
- optimise.md line ~540: same pattern
- README.md line ~22: already documents `get`, so verified-clean if the `get` form is already there

Add one line to SKILL.md noting that `tomlctl parse <file>` is a deprecated alias for `tomlctl get <file>` and may be removed in a future version.

**Preserve shared-block parity**: `parse` may appear inside SHARED-BLOCK:flow-context or SHARED-BLOCK:ledger-schema. If it does, change ALL FOUR copies atomically so `scripts/verify-shared-blocks.sh` still passes. If making these changes would require synchronised edits across 4 files that verify-shared-blocks.sh does not cover automatically, use `tomlctl blocks verify` (or the bash script) after your edits to confirm parity.

### R14 — reference `--array` flag in rollback_events docs (medium, completeness)
**Files**: `claude/commands/review-apply.md` (~line 645), `claude/commands/optimise-apply.md` (~line 606)
**Fix**: the Rust agent is adding `tomlctl items apply --array <name>`. Update the rollback_events step to show the canonical recipe using the new flag:

```bash
printf '%s' '{"timestamp":"2026-04-18T...","command":"review-apply","cause":"...","items":["R1"],"stash_ref":"stash@{0}"}' \
  | tomlctl items apply <ledger> --array rollback_events --ops '[{"op":"add","json":-}]'
```

Actually the ops format needs a value, not `-`, since the op's `json` field is the payload. Re-shape so the stdin carries the whole ops array:

```bash
printf '%s' '[{"op":"add","json":{"timestamp":"2026-04-18T...","command":"review-apply","cause":"...","items":["R1"],"stash_ref":"stash@{0}"}}]' \
  | tomlctl items apply <ledger> --array rollback_events --ops -
```

Document that `--array` is an apply-only flag, default `"items"`, and exists specifically to support `rollback_events` and any future ledger-level arrays-of-tables. Mirror the change in optimise-apply.md.

**Preserve shared-block parity**: this text likely lives in SHARED-BLOCK:ledger-schema (the Rollback event log subsection). If so, update all four command files atomically and re-run the parity check.

## Sequence of work

1. Re-read each target file in full before editing — preserve prose style and heading structure.
2. Start with R13 (smallest semantic change, helps you orient on all 4 command files).
3. Then R1 (add `--count` doc references — trivial now that you know the interface).
4. Then R11 (mechanical spelling pass).
5. Then R6 (sidecar doc clarity — localised to README + SKILL).

## Context7 MCP use — MANDATORY

For the SHARED-BLOCK extraction (R12 / R14) you need clarity on the shared-block marker format. Grep-and-read rather than Context7. For any references to external tools (jq, git, etc.) cited in the docs, no Context7 lookup needed — these are stable, widely-known commands.

## Important constraints

- **Do NOT edit `tomlctl/src/main.rs` or `tomlctl/Cargo.toml`** — the Rust agent owns those.
- Preserve existing markdown heading levels, table structures, and code-fence language tags.

- Tag every item with exactly one of `applied` / `verified-clean` / `skipped`.
- Report `deviation:` lines for any edit that crosses into a file not in this cluster's scope.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	set -euo pipefail
3	
4	cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)"
5	
6	MANIFEST="${MANIFEST:-scripts/shared-blocks.toml}"
7	
8	if [[ ! -f $MANIFEST ]]; then
9	  echo "error: manifest not found at $MANIFEST" >&2
10	  exit 2
11	fi
12	
13	if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
14	  HASHER='sha256sum'
15	elif command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
16	  HASHER='shasum -a 256'
17	else
18	  echo "error: need sha256sum or shasum -a 256 on PATH" >&2
19	  exit 2
20	fi
21	
22	hash_block() {
23	  local file=$1 name=$2
24	  awk -v start="<!-- SHARED-BLOCK:${name} START -->" \
25	      -v end="<!-- SHARED-BLOCK:${name} END -->" '
26	    $0 == start { in_block=1; next }
27	    $0 == end   { in_block=0; next }
28	    in_block    { print }
29	  ' "$file" | $HASHER | awk '{print $1}'
30	}
31	
32	pairs=$(awk '
33	  /^\[\[block\]\]/ { name=""; in_files=0; next }
34	  /^name = "/ {
35	    gsub(/^name = "|"$/, "")
36	    name=$0
37	    next
38	  }
39	  /^files = \[/ { in_files=1; next }
40	  in_files && /^\]/ { in_files=0; name=""; next }
41	  in_files && /^[[:space:]]*"[^"]+"/ {
42	    gsub(/^[[:space:]]*"|",?$|"$/, "")
43	    if (name != "") print name "\t" $0
44	  }
45	' "$MANIFEST")
46	
47	if [[ -z $pairs ]]; then
48	  echo "error: manifest yielded no (block, file) pairs — check $MANIFEST syntax" >&2
49	  exit 2
50	fi
51	
52	fail=0
53	declare -A first_hash first_file
54	
55	while IFS=$'\t' read -r bname bfile; do
56	  [[ -z $bname || -z $bfile ]] && continue
57	
58	  if [[ ! -f $bfile ]]; then
59	    echo "error: block '$bname' references missing file: $bfile" >&2
60	    fail=1
61	    continue
62	  fi
63	
64	  if ! grep -qF "<!-- SHARED-BLOCK:${bname} START -->" "$bfile"; then
65	    echo "error: $bfile missing START marker for block '$bname'" >&2
66	    fail=1
67	    continue
68	  fi
69	  if ! grep -qF "<!-- SHARED-BLOCK:${bname} END -->" "$bfile"; then
70	    echo "error: $bfile missing END marker for block '$bname'" >&2
71	    fail=1
72	    continue
73	  fi
74	
75	  h=$(hash_block "$bfile" "$bname")
76	
77	  if [[ -z ${first_hash[$bname]:-} ]]; then
78	    first_hash[$bname]=$h
79	    first_file[$bname]=$bfile
80	  elif [[ ${first_hash[$bname]} != "$h" ]]; then
81	    echo "error: block '$bname' drift:" >&2
82	    printf '  %s  hash=%s\n' "${first_file[$bname]}" "${first_hash[$bname]}" >&2
83	    printf '  %s  hash=%s\n' "$bfile" "$h" >&2
84	    fail=1
85	  fi
86	done <<< "$pairs"
87	
88	if [[ $fail -eq 0 ]]; then
89	  echo "shared-block parity: OK"
90	fi
91	exit $fail

7	## Flow Context
8	
9	All `.claude/...` paths below resolve to the **project-local** `.claude/` directory at the git top-level. If no git top-level is available, refuse rather than fall back to `~/.claude/`.
10	
11	### Canonical Flow Schema
12	
13	**No inline comments in the schema** — `Edit` tool's exact-string matching clobbers trailing comments during single-field updates. Status values and other enumerations are documented in the Shared Rules below, not in the schema block.
14	
15	```toml
16	slug = "auth-overhaul"
17	plan_path = "docs/plans/auth-overhaul.md"
18	status = "in-progress"
19	created = 2026-04-08
20	updated = 2026-04-16
21	branch = "auth-overhaul"
22	
23	scope = ["src/auth/**", "src/middleware/auth.rs"]
24	
25	[tasks]
26	total = 10
27	completed = 3
28	in_progress = 1
29	
30	[artifacts]
31	review_ledger = ".claude/flows/auth-overhaul/review-ledger.toml"
32	optimise_findings = ".claude/flows/auth-overhaul/optimise-findings.toml"
33	```
34	
35	### Shared Rules
36	
37	#### Status vocabulary
38	
39	`status` takes one of four string values: `draft`, `in-progress`, `review`, `complete`.
40	
41	- `draft` — written by `plan-new` at creation.
42	- `in-progress` — written by `implement` when it starts a task; written by `plan-update` after work resumes.
43	- `review` — written only by `plan-update` when a plan enters a review phase between implementation rounds.
44	- `complete` — written only by `plan-update` when all tasks are done or all remainders are deferred.
45	
46	**Unknown-value rule**: if a command reads a `status` it doesn't recognise, it MUST treat it as `in-progress` (fail-soft) and proceed. Do not error.
47	
48	#### Field responsibilities
49	
50	- `slug` — immutable after creation. Only `plan-new` writes it.
51	- `plan_path` — immutable after creation. For multi-file plans, `plan_path` points at the **outline file** (e.g. `docs/plans/auth-overhaul/00-outline.md`), not the directory.
52	- `created` — immutable after creation. **Every command that rewrites `context.toml` MUST preserve `created` verbatim.** Never regenerate it.
53	- `updated` — writeable by `plan-new`, `implement`, `plan-update`. Set to today's date (ISO 8601) on every write.
54	- `branch` — optional. `plan-new` sets it from `git branch --show-current` if that produces a non-empty string; otherwise the field is **omitted entirely** (not written as empty string). No other command writes `branch`. Resolution step 3 skips flows whose `branch` key is absent.
55	- `scope` — writeable by `plan-new` (initial derivation from the plan's "Affected areas" section, globs like `<dir>/**`) and by `plan-update reconcile` (may refine based on actual edits). Never empty after initial creation — if `plan-new` cannot derive anything, it writes the plan's affected directories as `<dir>/**` patterns.
56	- `[tasks]` — writeable by `plan-update` (all ops that touch progress); writeable by `implement` (`in_progress` counter only when starting/finishing).
57	- `[artifacts]` — **canonical, always written.** Paths are computed from `slug` but must be persisted in the TOML for stability. If `[artifacts]` is absent when read, commands compute from `slug` but MUST write it back on their next TOML write.
58	
59	#### Slug derivation
60	
61	Slug = plan filename minus `.md` extension. Examples:
62	- `docs/plans/auth-overhaul.md` → slug `auth-overhaul`
63	- `docs/plans/auth-overhaul/00-outline.md` (multi-file) → slug `auth-overhaul` (parent directory name)
64	
65	No additional slugification — the filename is already the slug.
66	
67	#### Flow resolution order (every command, every invocation)
68	
69	1. **Explicit `--flow <slug>` argument**. If provided, use it verbatim. If `.claude/flows/<slug>/` doesn't exist, error.
70	2. **Scope glob match on the path argument**. For each `.claude/flows/*/context.toml` where `status != "complete"`, read the `scope` array. For each pattern, invoke the `Glob` tool with the pattern and check whether the target path appears in the result. If exactly one flow matches, use it. Skip `status == "complete"` flows entirely.
71	3. **Git branch match**. Run `git branch --show-current`. If the output is non-empty, look for a flow whose `context.branch` equals it (exact match, case-sensitive). Skip this step if output is empty (detached HEAD).
72	4. **`.claude/active-flow` fallback**. Read the single-line slug. If `.claude/flows/<slug>/` exists with a valid `context.toml`, use it. If the pointed-at directory is missing or the TOML is malformed, proceed to step 5.
73	5. **Ambiguous / none found**: list candidate flows (all non-complete flows with summary: slug, plan_path, status), ask the user.
74	
75	#### TOML read/write contract
76	
77	- **Reading**: if `context.toml` is missing required fields (`slug`, `plan_path`, `status`, `created`, `updated`, `scope`, `[tasks]`, `[artifacts]`), prompt the user with the specific missing fields and the plan's current path. Do not synthesise defaults silently.
78	- **Reading**: if `context.toml` is syntactically invalid (can't be parsed as TOML), report the parse error and ask the user to fix manually. Do not attempt auto-repair.
79	- **Writing (preferred)**: use `tomlctl` (see skill `tomlctl`) — `tomlctl set <file> <key-path> <value>` for a scalar, `tomlctl set-json <file> <key-path> --json <value>` for arrays or sub-tables. `tomlctl` preserves `created` verbatim, preserves key order, holds an exclusive sidecar `.lock`, and writes atomically via tempfile + rename. One tool call per field — no Read/Edit choreography required.
80	- **Writing (fallback)**: if `tomlctl` is unavailable, Read the file, modify only the target line(s) via `Edit`, Write back. Preserve `created` verbatim. Preserve key order. Do not introduce inline comments.
81	
82	#### Flow-less fallback
83	
84	When `/review` or `/optimise` run on code outside any flow (resolution ends at step 5 and user picks "no flow"):
85	- `/review` → `.claude/reviews/<scope>.toml`
86	- `/optimise` → `.claude/optimise-findings/<scope>.toml`
87	
88	Slug derivation for flow-less scope: lowercase, replace `/\` with `-`, collapse `--`, strip leading `-` (preserved from pre-redesign).
89	
90	#### Completed-flow handling
91	
92	Flows with `status = "complete"` are skipped by resolution step 2 (scope glob match). They remain on disk for audit but do not participate in auto-resolution. Users can still target them via explicit `--flow <slug>`.
93	<!-- SHARED-BLOCK:flow-context END -->
94	
95	<!-- SHARED-BLOCK:ledger-schema START -->
96	## Ledger Schema
97	
98	All `.claude/...` ledger paths below — whether flow-local (`review-ledger.toml`, `optimise-findings.toml`) or flow-less (`.claude/reviews/<scope>.toml`, `.claude/optimise-findings/<scope>.toml`) — share the single canonical schema defined in this section. This section is embedded verbatim into `review.md`, `review-apply.md`, `optimise.md`, and `optimise-apply.md` so every command that reads or writes a ledger sees the same rules. Read this section before touching any ledger read/write logic.
99	
100	### Canonical Ledger Schema (single source of truth)
101	
102	Both `review-ledger.toml` and `optimise-findings.toml` share this schema. Required fields marked — others optional. No inline comments in emitted TOML.
103	
104	```toml
105	schema_version = 1
106	last_updated = 2026-04-16
107	
108	[[items]]
109	id = "R1"
110	file = "src/accounting/postings.rs"
111	line = 66
112	severity = "critical"
113	effort = "small"
114	category = "quality"
115	summary = "Trade sell wrong journal entries"
116	first_flagged = 2026-04-08
117	rounds = 1
118	status = "fixed"
119	resolved = 2026-04-08
120	resolution = "Gated with BooksError in ca44570"
121	flow = "warm-meandering-zebra"
122	
123	[[items]]
124	id = "R22"
125	file = "src/events/listeners.rs"
126	line = 84
127	symbol = "listeners::trigger"
128	severity = "suggestion"
129	effort = "small"

132	description = "Re-entrancy risk: pipeline mutex could deadlock if listeners call pipeline service."
133	first_flagged = 2026-04-08

140	
141	#### Required fields (every item)
142	
143	- `id` — `R{n}` for review items, `O{n}` for optimise items. Stable; never renumbered; monotonic per-ledger.
144	- `file` — repo-relative file path.
145	- `line` — integer. Use `0` if no specific line applies.
146	- `severity` — `critical` | `warning` | `suggestion`.
147	- `effort` — `trivial` | `small` | `medium`.
148	- `category` — see vocabulary below.
149	- `summary` — one-line description.
150	- `first_flagged` — TOML date, ISO 8601.
151	- `rounds` — integer, incremented each time the same issue is re-flagged in a later run.
152	- `status` — see disposition vocabulary below.
153	
154	#### Optional fields
155	
156	- `symbol` — function / struct / trait method name. **Strongly recommended** for line-drift resilience; omit if no natural anchor applies.
157	- `description` — longer explanation when `summary` is insufficient.
158	- `evidence` — array of strings: doc URLs, Context7 query citations, benchmark links.
159	- `related` — array of peer IDs (e.g. `["R5", "R8"]`).
160	- `flow` — slug of the flow that contains or resolved this item. Empty/omitted for flow-less ledgers.
161	- `depends_on` — array of ledger IDs (e.g. `["O7", "R12"]`) this item must apply AFTER. Consumed by the topological sort in `/review-apply` and `/optimise-apply` Step 3. Forward references to non-existent IDs are harmless — the topo sort restricts the DAG to the selected set — but `tomlctl items orphans <ledger>` surfaces dangling refs for hygiene (emits `{"id":...,"class":"dangling-dep","dangling_deps":[...]}` records alongside `missing-file` and `symbol-missing` classes).
162	- `fingerprint` — opaque string computed by `tomlctl` (not hand-authored). Produced by `tomlctl items find-duplicates --tier B` as a 16-char SHA-256 truncation over `file|summary|severity|category|symbol`; current ledgers leave this field absent. Consumers treat absence as "fingerprint not yet computed".
163	- `rollback_rationale` — string; present on items whose transition was reverted by a Step 5.5 rollback in `/review-apply` or `/optimise-apply`. Set when a rollback flips an item from `fixed`/`applied` back to `open`. Preserved across subsequent rounds so the rollback history surfaces in future reports.
164	- `reopen_rationale` — string; present on items whose status was transitioned from `deferred` back to `open` via the deferred-trigger reopen sweep (`/review` and `/optimise` Step 1). Captures the trigger event that fired.
165	
166	#### Disposition-specific fields (required only when status matches)
167	
168	- `status = "fixed"` / `status = "applied"`:
169	  - `resolved` (date, required)
170	  - `resolution` (string, required) — commit SHA + short description.
171	- `status = "deferred"`:
172	  - `defer_reason` (string, required)
173	  - `defer_trigger` (string, required) — concrete re-evaluation condition.
174	- `status = "wontfix"` / `status = "wontapply"`:
175	  - `wontfix_rationale` (string, required).
176	- `status = "verified-clean"`:
177	  - `verified_note` (string, required) — the audit note (e.g. "Round 2 (2026-04-14) — migrations.rs idioms already match").
178	
179	#### Category vocabularies
180	
181	- **Review** (`review-ledger.toml`): `quality` | `security` | `architecture` | `completeness` | `db` | `verified-clean` (reserved for items with `status = "verified-clean"`).
182	- **Optimise** (`optimise-findings.toml`): `memory` | `serialization` | `query` | `algorithm` | `concurrency`.
183	
184	**Unknown-value fail-soft rules** (mandatory):
185	- Unknown `status` → treat as `open`.
186	- Unknown `category` → treat as `quality` (review) or `memory` (optimise); write a one-line warning to the command's console output but do not error.
187	
188	#### Disposition vocabulary
189	
190	- `open` — active, needs resolution.
191	- `deferred` — not acting now, with a concrete re-eval trigger.
192	- `fixed` (review) / `applied` (optimise) — resolved with commit evidence.
193	- `wontfix` (review) / `wontapply` (optimise) — intentional non-action with rationale.
194	- `verified-clean` (review only) — explicitly audited and confirmed clean; kept to avoid re-flagging via dedup.
195	
196	#### Render-to-markdown contract
197	
198	Commands emit TOML as the authoritative artifact. For human-readable console output, commands render items as grouped markdown tables (severity-grouped for new-finding reports; disposition-grouped for full ledger views) inline in their response. The rendered markdown is not persisted.
199	
200	#### Rollback event log
201	
202	When `/review-apply` or `/optimise-apply` Step 5.5 reverts a batch of transitions, the protocol appends one `[[rollback_events]]` table to the ledger root:
203	
204	```toml
205	[[rollback_events]]
206	timestamp = 2026-04-17T14:32:00Z
207	command = "review-apply"
208	cause = "build failure on src/accounting/postings.rs:122"
209	items = ["R3", "R7"]
210	stash_ref = "stash@{0}"
211	```
212	
213	Fields:
214	- `timestamp` — ISO 8601 date-time (seconds precision).
215	- `command` — `"review-apply"` or `"optimise-apply"`.
216	- `cause` — short description (build fail, test regression, or claimed-applied-without-diff).
217	- `items` — array of ledger IDs that were reverted back to `status = "open"`.
218	- `stash_ref` — `git stash` reference for the rolled-back working-tree state so the user can recover the changes if desired.
219	
220	`[[rollback_events]]` is append-only; existing entries are never rewritten or deleted. If the log grows unwieldy, older entries may be archived manually by moving them to `<ledger>.rollback-history.toml`; no command automates this yet.
221	
222	### Ledger TOML read/write contract
223	
224	Applies to every read/write of `review-ledger.toml` and `optimise-findings.toml`. This contract is DIFFERENT from the `context.toml` contract (single-object file, line-edit-safe) because ledgers use arrays-of-tables which are fragile under line-based editing (two items with identical `status = "open"` / `rounds = 1` lines defeat the Edit tool uniqueness).
225	
226	#### Read rules
227	
228	- **Missing `schema_version`**: treat as `1` and write it back on the next write. This is the only silent-default allowed.
229	- **`schema_version > 1`**: halt and ask the user — we don't know this format.
230	- **Missing required item field**: flag the item in the console output as malformed, skip it for resolution / dedup; do NOT attempt auto-repair.
231	- **TOML parse error**: report the error location; do NOT attempt auto-repair; ask the user to fix or restore from backup.
232	
233	#### Write strategy (MANDATORY)
234	
235	**Ledger writes MUST use parse-rewrite, not line-edit.** Preferred path — `tomlctl` (see skill `tomlctl`):
236	
237	- `tomlctl items add <ledger> --json '{...}'` — append a new item.
238	- `tomlctl items update <ledger> <id> --json '{...}'` — patch fields on an existing item matched by `id`.
239	- `tomlctl items remove <ledger> <id>` — delete by id.
240	- `tomlctl items apply <ledger> --ops '[{"op":"add|update|remove", ...}, ...]'` — batch multiple ops in one atomic, all-or-nothing file rewrite. Use this whenever touching several items in the same run so the ledger pays one parse + one write instead of N.
241	- `tomlctl set <ledger> last_updated <YYYY-MM-DD>` — bump the file-level `last_updated`.
242	- `tomlctl items next-id <ledger> --prefix R|O` — compute the next monotonic id.
243	- **Stdin for `--ops` / `--json`**: every JSON-accepting flag above treats `-` as a sentinel meaning "read JSON from stdin" — e.g. `printf '%s' "$OPS" | tomlctl items apply <ledger> --ops -`. Prefer this for large batches or payloads containing shell metacharacters (embedded quotes, `$`, backticks, or newlines in agent-produced `resolution` / `wontfix_rationale` / `verified_note` strings); avoids the tempfile round-trip and eliminates the argv-level quoting surface entirely. Empty stdin errors clearly.
244	
245	`tomlctl` writes go through `tempfile::NamedTempFile::persist` (atomic rename) and hold an exclusive advisory lock on a sidecar `.lock` file, so concurrent invocations are safe and an interrupted write cannot corrupt the ledger.
246	
247	**Fallback if `tomlctl` is unavailable** (missing binary, Rust not installed):
248	
249	1. Read the whole ledger file.
250	2. Parse it with `python3 -c "import tomllib; tomllib.load(open(PATH, 'rb'))"` (or an equivalent runtime — `python3` is assumed present on Linux; check CLAUDE.md `Build & test` section for alternatives if not).
251	3. Mutate the parsed structure in memory (add an item, change a status, increment `rounds`, etc.).
252	4. Serialise the whole structure back to TOML (preserve key order within each item per the convention below).
253	5. `Write` the new TOML over the old file in a single call.
254	
255	**Last-resort fallback** (python3 also unavailable, and the change is a single trivial edit):
256	- Read → use `Edit` with a unique surrounding context (include the preceding `id = "R{n}"` line in the match pattern to ensure uniqueness within the file).
257	- If `Edit` fails due to ambiguity: escalate to one of the parse-rewrite paths rather than approximating the match.
258	
259	#### Key-order convention (for serialisers that don't preserve order)
260	
261	When re-serialising an item, emit keys in this order:
262	`id, file, line, symbol, severity, effort, category, summary, description, evidence, first_flagged, rounds, related, status, <disposition-specific fields>, flow`
263	
264	The file-level keys come first: `schema_version`, `last_updated`, then `[[items]]` entries. `schema_version` MUST be preserved on every write.
265	
266	### Item-ID assignment and dedup
267	
268	- **ID assignment**: R-numbers for review items, O-numbers for optimise items. New items get `max(existing) + 1`. Never renumber. IDs retired by deletion are never reused.
269	- **Dedup rule (same for new-item merge AND regression detection)**: two findings match iff they have the **same `file`** AND (**same non-empty `symbol`** OR **exact `summary` string match**). No fuzzy matching, no keyword clustering. When in doubt, new ID.
270	- **Merge behaviour**:
271	  - New finding matches an `open` item → reuse the existing ID; increment `rounds`; update `last_updated` of the ledger.
272	  - New finding matches a `fixed` / `applied` item → **regression**; assign a new ID; write `related = ["<old id>"]`; flag prominently in the console report.
273	  - New finding matches a `deferred` / `wontfix` / `wontapply` / `verified-clean` item → treat as existing (no change); do not emit a new item; do not increment `rounds`. Note in console: "this matches an existing <status> item, not re-reporting."
274	- **Chronic-item escalation**: `rounds >= 3` on `open` items escalates in the summary output.
275	<!-- SHARED-BLOCK:ledger-schema END -->

277	# Code Review
278	
279	Review code for issues, incomplete work, opportunities for improvement, violations of DRY, non-idiomatic language usage, project structure violations, and disregard for good patterns in the existing codebase.
280	
281	Works in two modes:
282	- **Targeted** — pass file paths, directories, or a feature/area name as arguments (e.g. `/review src/api/endpoints/` or `/review auth`)
283	- **Recent changes** — with no arguments, automatically scopes to recently changed files
284	
285	> **Effort**: Requires `xhigh` or `max` — lower effort may reduce agent spawning and tool usage.
286	
287	## Step 1: Determine Scope and Load Prior Findings
288	
289	**Reason thoroughly through scope analysis.** Determine which files are in scope, how they relate, what classification each agent needs, and what prior review findings exist.
290	
291	### Resolve Flow
292	
293	Before anything else, run the **5-step flow resolution order** from the Shared Rules (above) to determine whether this review sits inside an active flow:
294	
295	1. Explicit `--flow <slug>` argument.
296	2. Scope glob match on the path argument against each non-complete `.claude/flows/*/context.toml`.
297	3. Git branch match against `context.branch`.
298	4. `.claude/active-flow` fallback.
299	5. Ambiguous / none found — list candidate flows and ask the user (or the user picks "no flow").
300	
301	**Batched tool calls**: emit the independent tool calls in this step (file `Read`s, `git` probes, `tomlctl` reads) in a **single response message** so they execute concurrently. Opus 4.7 handles the batch without context pressure; serialising these reads wastes round-trip budget. The only sequential dependency is that the ledger load (`tomlctl parse` / `tomlctl items list`) consumes the flow path resolved above — resolve the flow first, then batch everything else.
302	
303	If a flow resolves, record its `slug`, `scope`, `context.updated`, and `artifacts.review_ledger` — these are consumed by the staleness pre-check, the ledger load, and later persistence. If no flow resolves (step 5 yields "no flow"), proceed with flow-less behaviour as described in the Shared Rules' flow-less fallback.
304	
305	### Staleness Pre-Check
306	
307	If a flow resolved AND `status == "in-progress"` AND `git log -1 --format=%cI -- <scope paths>` returns a commit timestamp newer than `context.updated`, invoke the `plan-update` skill with the literal argument string `reconcile` via the `Skill` tool **before** proceeding to agent launch. The reconcile brings `context.updated`, `[tasks]` counts, and `scope` back in line with the actual state of the repo so the review runs against accurate prior context.
308	
309	Skip this check when no flow resolved, when `status != "in-progress"`, or when `git log` returns no matching commits (scope paths clean relative to `context.updated`).
310	
311	### Identify Files
312	
313	1. **If $ARGUMENTS specifies file paths, directories, glob patterns, or a feature/area name**, use that as the primary scope. For directories, include all source files recursively. For feature/area names (e.g. "cash management", "auth", "compliance"), use Grep and Glob to identify the relevant files across the codebase.
314	2. **If $ARGUMENTS is empty or only specifies a focus lens**, detect scope from git: on a feature branch use `git diff --name-only $(git merge-base HEAD main)..HEAD` (try `main`, fall back to `master`), otherwise use `git diff --name-only HEAD~1`. Also include `git diff --name-only` for unstaged changes.
315	3. If no files are found from either approach, ask the user what to review.
316	4. Classify each file by area (backend service, API endpoint, frontend component, infrastructure, config, etc.) — share this classification with all agents so they can focus on what's relevant to their lens.
317	
318	### Scope classification delegation
319	
320	When `Identify Files` yields more than 10 files (and the small-diff shortcut — ≤ 3 files — does NOT fire), delegate scope classification to an `Explore` agent (`subagent_type: "Explore"`, `thoroughness: "quick"`) to reclaim orchestrator context for Step 2 and beyond.
321	
322	The Explore agent MUST:
323	- Read `CLAUDE.md` at the repo top-level plus any per-subdirectory `CLAUDE.md` that falls under the scope.
324	- Classify each in-scope file by area (backend service, API endpoint, frontend component, infrastructure, config, test).
325	- Extract CLAUDE.md excerpts relevant to review: declared tech stack, architectural conventions, and any `## Review Focus` section if present.
326	- Return a compact classification table (roughly 20 words per file) and CLAUDE.md excerpts — **under 600 words total**.
327	
328	Example return format:
329	
330	```
331	| file                        | area          | notes                                 |
332	|-----------------------------|---------------|---------------------------------------|
333	| src/api/endpoints/auth.rs   | API endpoint  | uses actix-web; auth middleware layer |
334	| src/domain/user.rs          | backend core  | no framework deps                     |
335	| ...                         |               |                                       |
336	
337	CLAUDE.md excerpts:
338	- Tech stack: Rust 1.75, actix-web 4, sqlx 0.7, Postgres
339	- Review focus: strict no-unwrap in request handlers
340	```
341	
342	The orchestrator keeps only the table and excerpts; raw file reads stay in the Explore agent's context. Skip the delegation when scope ≤ 10 files — the inline classification in `Identify Files` suffices at that size, and the delegation overhead dwarfs the context saved.
343	
344	The delegation does NOT replace `Identify Files` — it augments it. File discovery (git diff / glob / feature-name search) still runs in the main thread; only the read-intensive per-file classification is delegated.
345	
346	### Load Review Ledger
347	
348	The ledger path comes from the resolved flow's `context.toml`:
349	
350	- **Flow resolved** → read the path from `context.toml.artifacts.review_ledger` (canonical location is `.claude/flows/<slug>/review-ledger.toml`). If `[artifacts]` is absent for any reason, compute the path from `slug` as `.claude/flows/<slug>/review-ledger.toml` and write it back on the next TOML write per the Shared Rules contract.
351	- **No flow (flow-less fallback)** → write to `.claude/reviews/<scope>.toml`. Derive `<scope>` per the flow-less slug rule in the Flow Context block above (line 87). Examples:
352	  - `/review src/api/endpoints/` → `.claude/reviews/src-api-endpoints.toml`
353	  - `/review auth` → `.claude/reviews/auth.toml`
354	  - Git-derived scope (no args) → use the branch name; `.claude/reviews/recent.toml` if on the main branch
355	  - Single file → `.claude/reviews/src-utils-helpers.toml`
356	
357	Check for the ledger file at the resolved path and load it per the **Ledger TOML read/write contract** in the `## Ledger Schema` section above:
358	
359	- **File missing** → this is a first review. Initialise an in-memory ledger with `schema_version = 1`, `last_updated = <today>`, `items = []`. Do not write to disk yet — persistence happens in Step 3 after findings are consolidated.
360	- **File present** → parse it via `tomlctl --verify-integrity parse <file>` (whole doc) or `tomlctl --verify-integrity items list <file> --status open` to pre-filter to just the open items this step needs (falls back to `python3 -c "import tomllib; tomllib.load(open(PATH, 'rb'))"` if `tomlctl` is unavailable). The `--verify-integrity` global flag checks the `<file>.sha256` sidecar before parsing; on digest mismatch tomlctl errors with both expected and actual hashes and never auto-repairs — surface the error to the user and halt. Skip `--verify-integrity` only when the sidecar is known-absent (first-ever run for this ledger; `tomlctl` will have written one on that run's final write). Apply the read rules from the Ledger TOML read/write contract:
361	  - Missing `schema_version` → treat as `1`, note that it will be written back on next write.
362	  - `schema_version > 1` → halt and ask the user.
363	  - Any `[[items]]` entry missing a required field → flag as malformed in console output, exclude it from dedup/resolution for this run, do NOT attempt auto-repair.
364	  - TOML parse error → report the error location and ask the user to fix or restore from backup; do NOT attempt auto-repair.
365	
366	**Clock-skew / backdated `last_updated` validation**: after reading the ledger, compare `last_updated` against today's date plus `git log -1 --format=%cI`'s latest in-scope commit. If `last_updated` is more than 1 day ahead of both (i.e. future-dated beyond plausible clock skew), emit a one-line warning to the console (`ledger last_updated=<date> is future-dated; treating as today for filter purposes`) and use today for any legacy-numeric selector resolution in /review-apply. Do not error — the ledger may be correct; just don't let future dates silently drop items from the latest-report filter.
367	
368	From the loaded ledger, extract all items whose `file` overlaps with the current scope. This is the **prior findings context** — pass it to every agent so they can:
369	- Skip items already tracked as `fixed`, `applied`, `wontfix`, `wontapply`, `deferred`, or `verified-clean` (these carry their disposition; do not re-emit them)
370	- Flag items tracked as `fixed` that appear to have **regressed** (the same issue is present again) — this becomes a new item with `related = ["<old id>"]` per the dedup rules
371	- Avoid re-reporting `open` items unless they've worsened — instead, note "still present" if relevant; the merge step will reuse the existing ID and increment `rounds`
372	
373	If no ledger was loaded, this is a first review — proceed without prior context.
374	
375	### Orphan surfacing (read-only)
376	
377	After the ledger loads and before scoping the agent launch, walk every `[[items]]` entry in the resolved ledger whose `status == "open"` and report orphans to the console without auto-transitioning:
378	
379	- **File orphan**: the item's `file` path no longer exists. Detect via a single `Glob` call per unique path, or — for small ledgers — a batched `Test-Path` / `[ -e <path> ]` check.
380	- **Symbol orphan**: the item has a non-empty `symbol` field and a `Grep` for that symbol (name-only, not exact-match) against the current file tree returns no results. Use one `Grep` call with `output_mode: "files_with_matches"` over the repo to avoid per-item lookups.
381	
382	For each orphan, emit a one-line console note in Step 3's report:
383	
384	```
385	orphan R7 — file `src/old-module.rs` no longer present (check for rename; run /review if the work has moved)
386	orphan R12 — symbol `foo_bar` not found anywhere in the repo (likely renamed; re-run /review at the new location)
387	```
388	
389	Orphans surface, they do NOT auto-transition. The ledger ID is preserved — symbol renames and file moves do not invalidate disposition history. Prefer `tomlctl items orphans <ledger>` over a hand-rolled Glob/Grep walk — the subcommand emits a JSON array of `{id, class, file, symbol?, dangling_deps?}` records (classes: `missing-file`, `symbol-missing`, `dangling-dep`) in one call, keeping the orchestrator's Read budget free for Step 2. Render the returned records as console one-liners per the format above.
390	
391	### Deferred-item reopen sweep
392	
393	After orphan surfacing and before Step 2, walk every `[[items]]` entry with `status = "deferred"` and check whether each item's `defer_trigger` has fired. Known trigger forms (literal substring match on `defer_trigger`):
394	
395	- `after <path> exists` → test `[ -e <path> ]` (or `Test-Path <path>` on Windows).
396	- `after <file>:<symbol> landed` → test `<file>` exists AND `grep -qF "<symbol>" <file>` finds a match.
397	- `when <id> resolves` → look up `<id>` in the same ledger; fires when its `status` is any of `fixed`, `applied`, `verified-clean`, `wontfix`, or `wontapply`.
398	- `after <branch> merges` → test `git merge-base --is-ancestor <branch> HEAD`.
399	- `after <YYYY-MM-DD>` → fires when today's ISO date is ≥ the embedded date.
400	- Any other free-text trigger → surface to the console as a reminder; do not attempt automated detection.
401	
402	For each fired trigger, prompt the user with the item's `id`, `summary`, and the matched trigger text:
403	
404	```
405	deferred R{n} — trigger fired: <matched trigger>
406	  summary: <R{n}.summary>
407	Reopen?
408	  [y] reopen (status → open, reopen_rationale recorded)
409	  [n] skip (leave deferred)
410	  [a] abort sweep (do not inspect further candidates)
411	```
412	
413	On `[y]`, queue the transition for a single atomic `tomlctl items apply --ops -` at the end of the sweep: set `status = "open"`, preserve `defer_reason` (audit trail), drop `defer_trigger`, set `reopen_rationale = "trigger fired: <matched trigger text>"`. Never auto-transition silently — every reopen passes through the prompt.
414	
415	Non-interactive invocations surface candidates only (`found N deferred items with fired triggers; re-run interactively to reopen`) and do not mutate the ledger.
416	
417	**Small-diff shortcut**: If 3 or fewer files are in scope, launch a single comprehensive review agent instead of four specialized ones. Give it all four lenses, all mandatory tool-use requirements (Context7 and WebSearch), the prior findings context, and a cap of 15 findings.
418	
419	### Design Note: Intentional Asymmetry with `/optimise`
420	
421	`/review` has no counterpart to `/optimise`'s Step 1.5 Focal Points Brief. The asymmetry is intentional. `/optimise`'s five lenses (Memory, Serialization, Queries, Algorithm, Async) are runtime-specific — performance concerns hinge on async runtime, serialization strategy, query engine, and compilation target, which the orchestrator must pre-digest so agents can reason about the right things. `/review`'s four lenses (Quality, Security, Architecture, Completeness) are language-agnostic — idioms, authorization models, layering discipline, and test coverage apply across technology stacks without needing project-specific focal framing.
422	
423	The `/review` agent prompts already include CLAUDE.md's tech stack and the prior-findings context in Step 1; that's sufficient to steer the lens. Adding a focal-points synthesis step would duplicate prior-findings context without adding signal. This asymmetry is intentional — future `/review` passes over this command should not re-flag it as "/review lacks focal-points synthesis" (the mirror of this note in `optimise.md` explains why that command has no small-diff agent-collapse shortcut).
424	
425	## Step 2: Launch Parallel Review Agents
426	
427	### Task tracking (runtime only)
428	
429	Before launching review agents, call `TaskCreate` once per lens: Quality, Security, Architecture, Completeness — 4 tasks for a normal run, OR 1 task for the small-diff shortcut (≤ 3 files, single combined agent). Each task's `subject` names the lens plus a scope summary (e.g. `Security: src/api/*`); `description` is one line of the file list and classification relevant to that lens.
430	
431	As agents transition, call `TaskUpdate` to move each task `pending → in_progress → completed` on launch and return. Do NOT mint per-finding tasks — that shadows the ledger, which is the persistent source of truth for per-item state. Do NOT hand tasks forward to `/review-apply`: tasks are ephemeral to this run while the ledger persists across commands.
432

451	### Agent 1: Code Quality, DRY, Idioms & Pattern Conformance
452	
453	Look at the changed code through the lens of code quality, consistency, and idiomatic correctness. This agent has two complementary concerns:
454	
455	**Internal consistency** — Search the broader codebase for similar logic, patterns, and conventions. Does the new code follow the same idioms as existing code — or does it introduce duplication or a different way of doing things? Consider naming, structure, complexity, and whether the code would be easy for another developer to understand. Refer to CLAUDE.md for documented conventions, but also look at actual code to see what patterns are established in practice.
456	
457	**Idiomatic language usage** — Evaluate whether the code uses language and framework features the way they are intended. This means reviewing against the idioms of the specific languages and frameworks in use, not just internal project conventions. Identify what languages, frameworks, and runtimes the project uses, then check the changed code against their established idioms and best practices. Use Context7 MCP tools to verify idiomatic API usage when uncertain. Look for:
458	- Preferring language builtins and standard library facilities over manual reimplementations
459	- Using type system features properly (e.g., sum types, generics, type narrowing) rather than working around them
460	- Following the framework's intended patterns rather than fighting against its design
461	- Using modern language features where the project's target runtime supports them
462	- Avoiding anti-patterns documented in official language or framework style guides
463	- Using runtime-specific APIs where they offer meaningful advantages over generic alternatives

465	Do NOT flag: minor style differences that don't affect readability, single-use helper functions that aid clarity, patterns that are intentionally different due to different requirements, or older idioms that are consistent with the rest of the codebase (consistency trumps modernity unless the project is actively migrating).

494	## Interim checkpoint
495	
496	After all review agents return but BEFORE rendering the final findings report, persist new items (and any reopened items from the deferred-reopen sweep) to the ledger in a single atomic `tomlctl items apply --ops -` call. Rationale: an interrupted run (Ctrl-C between agent return and Step 3 render) would otherwise lose the review output. Writing a checkpoint at this boundary makes findings durable the moment they exist. The Step 1 idempotency guards (open items reuse via dedup; resolved items skip re-flagging) make a re-run safe — the worst case is re-rendering a report from an already-checkpointed ledger.
497	
498	Defer two writes to the final render in Step 3: (1) `tomlctl set <ledger> last_updated <today>` — the ledger is only "fresh" when the report was actually produced; (2) `rounds` increments for existing open items — these only matter once the report includes them. The checkpoint covers inserts + ledger-confirmed transitions (new items from agent output, deferred-item reopens confirmed by user prompt); scalar bookkeeping stays in the final render.
499	
500	Skip the checkpoint entirely if no transitions are pending (agents returned no new items AND the deferred-reopen sweep produced no confirmed reopens). One `tomlctl items list --count` suffices — do not emit an empty `--ops` payload.

502	## Step 3: Consolidate and Persist
503	
504	**Reason thoroughly through consolidation.** Cross-reference all agent results, deduplicate overlapping findings, resolve conflicting assessments, cross-reference with the prior findings context, and synthesize into a coherent report.
505	
506	### Assign Finding IDs
507	
508	Apply the dedup, merge, and regression rules from the `## Ledger Schema` section (Item-ID assignment and dedup). In short:
509	
510	- **Dedup rule**: two findings match iff they share the **same `file`** AND (**same non-empty `symbol`** OR **exact `summary` string match**). No fuzzy matching.
511	- For each consolidated agent finding, check it against every item in the loaded ledger:
512	  - **Matches an `open` item** → reuse the existing `id`; the merge step will increment `rounds` and refresh `last_updated`. Do not mint a new ID.
513	  - **Matches a `fixed` item** → **regression**. Mint a new `R{n}` ID (continuing from `max(existing) + 1`); record `related = ["<old id>"]` on the new item; flag the regression prominently in the console report.
514	  - **Matches a `deferred` / `wontfix` / `verified-clean` item** → do NOT mint a new ID; do NOT emit the finding to the report as a new item; note in console output: "this matches an existing <status> item, not re-reporting." The existing item is left untouched (no `rounds` increment).
515	  - **No match** → mint a new `R{n}` ID = `max(existing R-numbers) + 1`. If the ledger is empty, start at `R1`.
516	- **Never renumber**. IDs are stable across rounds and are referenced by `/implement`, `/plan-update`, and disposition commands. IDs retired by deletion are never reused.
517	- **Chronic-item escalation**: any existing `open` item whose `rounds` will reach `3` or more after this round's merge MUST be called out separately in the summary output.

576	### Update the Review Ledger
577	
578	Persist the merged state to the ledger file at the path resolved in Step 1 — `context.toml.artifacts.review_ledger` for flows, or `.claude/reviews/<scope>.toml` for flow-less runs. Follow the **Ledger TOML read/write contract** from the `## Ledger Schema` section: **parse-rewrite, not line-edit.**
579	
580	**Primary write path — the two-call pattern:**
581	
582	1. Build the full list of mutations in memory from the merged round state — every class below becomes one entry in a single `ops` array:
583	   - **New finding, no dedup match** → `add` op for a new `[[items]]` with `id = R{next}`, `first_flagged = <today>`, `rounds = 1`, `status = "open"`.
584	   - **New finding matches a prior `open` item** → `update` op on that `id`: increment `rounds`; refresh `line` if it drifted; leave `first_flagged` untouched.
585	   - **Regression** (new finding matches a prior `fixed` item) → `add` op with a fresh ID, `related = ["<old id>"]`, `rounds = 1`, `status = "open"`. Do not mutate the prior `fixed` item.
586	   - **Prior `open` item confirmed fixed by agents** → `update` op: `status = "fixed"`, `resolved = <today>`, `resolution = "<commit SHA or short description>"`. Keep `first_flagged` and `rounds`.
587	   - **Prior `open` item not found in current scope** → no op (item is out of scope for this review, not resolved — leave untouched).
588	2. Apply the whole batch in ONE call: `tomlctl items apply <ledger> --ops '[...]'`.
589	3. Stamp the header in ONE call: `tomlctl set <ledger> last_updated <YYYY-MM-DD>`.
590	
591	`schema_version` MUST be preserved verbatim on every write (`tomlctl` does this automatically — never re-emit or modify it). Do NOT delete the ledger file.
592	
593	**Fallback — if `tomlctl` is unavailable:** use the python3 parse-rewrite recipe from the Ledger Schema contract (`python3 -c "import tomllib; ..."` to load, mutate the Python dict, serialise back with a TOML writer that preserves the key-order convention — `tomli_w` or equivalent — then a single whole-file `Write` call).
594	
595	**Mutations to apply for this round:**
596	
597	- Set `last_updated = <today>` (TOML date, ISO 8601).
598	- **New finding, no dedup match** → append a new `[[items]]` entry with `id = R{next}`, `first_flagged = <today>`, `rounds = 1`, `status = "open"`, plus all required fields from the agent finding. `flow = <slug>` when a flow resolved; omit otherwise.
599	- **New finding matches a prior `open` item** (same `file` AND (same non-empty `symbol` OR exact `summary` match)) → mutate that item: increment `rounds` by 1; refresh `line` if it drifted; leave `first_flagged` untouched.
600	- **Prior `open` item not found in current scope** → leave the item untouched (it is out of scope for this review, not resolved).
601	- **Prior `open` item confirmed fixed by agents** → mutate the item's `status = "fixed"` with `resolved = <today>` and `resolution = "<commit SHA or short description>"`. Keep `first_flagged` and `rounds`.
602	- **Regression** (new finding matches a prior `fixed` item) → append a new `[[items]]` entry with a fresh ID, `related = ["<old id>"]`, `rounds = 1`, `status = "open"`. Do not mutate the prior `fixed` item.
603	
604	**Chronic-item handling**: items whose `rounds >= 3` after mutation are reported in the console escalation callout (see Produce the Review Report). The ledger carries no extra chronic flag — the `rounds` count is the source of truth.

606	### Prompt for Action
607	
608	After presenting the report, prompt the user with actionable next steps based on what was found:
609

611	  *"Run `/review-apply R4,R7` to address the quick wins."*
612	  (`/implement` remains available for plan-task-driven work that goes beyond a single review finding.)
613	- If there are findings suitable for deferral:
614	  *"To defer items: reply with `defer R4 — reason — re-evaluate trigger`."*
615	- If there are findings to dismiss:
616	  *"To dismiss items as intentional: reply with `wontfix R7 — rationale`."*
617	- If items have `Rounds >= 3`:
618	  *"R3 has appeared in 3 consecutive reviews without being addressed. Consider prioritizing it or explicitly deferring with a trigger."*

620	## Step 4: Handle Dispositions (if user responds)
621	
622	If the user responds with disposition commands in the same conversation (these are conversational commands, not slash-command invocations — recognize them by pattern), apply the corresponding in-place TOML mutation to the ledger via parse-rewrite (per the `## Ledger Schema` section's Ledger TOML read/write contract). Update `last_updated = <today>` on every disposition write.
623	
624	- **`defer R{n} — reason — trigger`** → locate the item with `id = "R{n}"`; set `status = "deferred"`, `defer_reason = "<reason>"`, `defer_trigger = "<trigger>"`. Both `defer_reason` and `defer_trigger` are required when `status = "deferred"`.
625	- **`wontfix R{n} — rationale`** → locate the item with `id = "R{n}"`; set `status = "wontfix"`, `wontfix_rationale = "<rationale>"`.
626	- **`fix R{n}`** → look up the item's `file`, `line`, and `summary` (plus `description` if present) from the ledger; route to `/implement` with the expanded description. **Do NOT mutate `status` here** — the resolution transition (`status = "fixed"` with `resolved` + `resolution`) happens when the fix actually lands, either via the deviation protocol inside `/implement` or via a subsequent `/plan-update` invocation. `/review` only writes the `fixed` status when a later run detects the issue is no longer present (see "Update the Review Ledger").
627	
628	Apply the mutation immediately with ONE `tomlctl items update` call per disposition — e.g. `tomlctl items update <ledger> R{n} --json '{"status":"deferred","defer_reason":"...","defer_trigger":"..."}'`. Follow with `tomlctl set <ledger> last_updated <YYYY-MM-DD>`.
629	
630	## Important Constraints
631	
632	- **Parse-rewrite, not line-edit** — ledger writes MUST follow the Ledger TOML read/write contract in the `## Ledger Schema` section. `[[items]]` arrays of tables defeat line-based editing uniqueness once more than one `open` / `rounds = 1` item exists. Use `tomlctl items add|update|remove|apply` (preferred) or fall back to `python3 -c "import tomllib; ..."` + mutate + serialise + single `Write` call.
633	- **Don't auto-dispose** — never set `status = "wontfix"` or `status = "deferred"` without explicit user instruction. Items stay `status = "open"` until the user dispositions them or a later review run verifies the issue is fixed.
634	- **Scope-aware ledger queries** — only surface prior items whose `file` overlaps with the current review scope. Don't report on items outside the current review.
635	- **Ledger item is lightweight** — `summary` is the one-line identifier; put longer prose in `description` only when `summary` genuinely isn't enough. Do not store full code snippets — reference by `file` + `line` + `symbol`.
636	- **Chronic item escalation** — items with `rounds >= 3` (post-merge) MUST be called out explicitly in the summary, not buried in the tables. These represent a pattern of findings being ignored.
637	- **ID stability** — once an item gets an R-number it is permanent. Never renumber. If a finding is resolved (`status = "fixed"`) and a similar issue appears later matching by `file` + `symbol`/`summary`, the new occurrence is a **regression** and gets a new R-number with `related = ["<old id>"]`; the old item stays `status = "fixed"`.
638	- **Render-to-markdown is ephemeral** — the markdown tables in the Review Summary are for console display only. The TOML ledger is the single persistent artifact.

35	### Shared Rules
36	
37	#### Status vocabulary
38	
39	`status` takes one of four string values: `draft`, `in-progress`, `review`, `complete`.
40	
41	- `draft` — written by `plan-new` at creation.
42	- `in-progress` — written by `implement` when it starts a task; written by `plan-update` after work resumes.
43	- `review` — written only by `plan-update` when a plan enters a review phase between implementation rounds.
44	- `complete` — written only by `plan-update` when all tasks are done or all remainders are deferred.
45	
46	**Unknown-value rule**: if a command reads a `status` it doesn't recognise, it MUST treat it as `in-progress` (fail-soft) and proceed. Do not error.
47	
48	#### Field responsibilities
49	
50	- `slug` — immutable after creation. Only `plan-new` writes it.
51	- `plan_path` — immutable after creation. For multi-file plans, `plan_path` points at the **outline file** (e.g. `docs/plans/auth-overhaul/00-outline.md`), not the directory.
52	- `created` — immutable after creation. **Every command that rewrites `context.toml` MUST preserve `created` verbatim.** Never regenerate it.
53	- `updated` — writeable by `plan-new`, `implement`, `plan-update`. Set to today's date (ISO 8601) on every write.
54	- `branch` — optional. `plan-new` sets it from `git branch --show-current` if that produces a non-empty string; otherwise the field is **omitted entirely** (not written as empty string). No other command writes `branch`. Resolution step 3 skips flows whose `branch` key is absent.
55	- `scope` — writeable by `plan-new` (initial derivation from the plan's "Affected areas" section, globs like `<dir>/**`) and by `plan-update reconcile` (may refine based on actual edits). Never empty after initial creation — if `plan-new` cannot derive anything, it writes the plan's affected directories as `<dir>/**` patterns.
56	- `[tasks]` — writeable by `plan-update` (all ops that touch progress); writeable by `implement` (`in_progress` counter only when starting/finishing).
57	- `[artifacts]` — **canonical, always written.** Paths are computed from `slug` but must be persisted in the TOML for stability. If `[artifacts]` is absent when read, commands compute from `slug` but MUST write it back on their next TOML write.
58	
59	#### Slug derivation
60	
61	Slug = plan filename minus `.md` extension. Examples:
62	- `docs/plans/auth-overhaul.md` → slug `auth-overhaul`
63	- `docs/plans/auth-overhaul/00-outline.md` (multi-file) → slug `auth-overhaul` (parent directory name)
64	
65	No additional slugification — the filename is already the slug.
66	
67	#### Flow resolution order (every command, every invocation)
68	
69	1. **Explicit `--flow <slug>` argument**. If provided, use it verbatim. If `.claude/flows/<slug>/` doesn't exist, error.
70	2. **Scope glob match on the path argument**. For each `.claude/flows/*/context.toml` where `status != "complete"`, read the `scope` array. For each pattern, invoke the `Glob` tool with the pattern and check whether the target path appears in the result. If exactly one flow matches, use it. Skip `status == "complete"` flows entirely.
71	3. **Git branch match**. Run `git branch --show-current`. If the output is non-empty, look for a flow whose `context.branch` equals it (exact match, case-sensitive). Skip this step if output is empty (detached HEAD).
72	4. **`.claude/active-flow` fallback**. Read the single-line slug. If `.claude/flows/<slug>/` exists with a valid `context.toml`, use it. If the pointed-at directory is missing or the TOML is malformed, proceed to step 5.
73	5. **Ambiguous / none found**: list candidate flows (all non-complete flows with summary: slug, plan_path, status), ask the user.
74	
75	#### TOML read/write contract
76	
77	- **Reading**: if `context.toml` is missing required fields (`slug`, `plan_path`, `status`, `created`, `updated`, `scope`, `[tasks]`, `[artifacts]`), prompt the user with the specific missing fields and the plan's current path. Do not synthesise defaults silently.
78	- **Reading**: if `context.toml` is syntactically invalid (can't be parsed as TOML), report the parse error and ask the user to fix manually. Do not attempt auto-repair.
79	- **Writing (preferred)**: use `tomlctl` (see skill `tomlctl`) — `tomlctl set <file> <key-path> <value>` for a scalar, `tomlctl set-json <file> <key-path> --json <value>` for arrays or sub-tables. `tomlctl` preserves `created` verbatim, preserves key order, holds an exclusive sidecar `.lock`, and writes atomically via tempfile + rename. One tool call per field — no Read/Edit choreography required.
80	- **Writing (fallback)**: if `tomlctl` is unavailable, Read the file, modify only the target line(s) via `Edit`, Write back. Preserve `created` verbatim. Preserve key order. Do not introduce inline comments.
81	
82	#### Flow-less fallback
83	
84	When `/review` or `/optimise` run on code outside any flow (resolution ends at step 5 and user picks "no flow"):
85	- `/review` → `.claude/reviews/<scope>.toml`

96	## Ledger Schema
97	
98	All `.claude/...` ledger paths below — whether flow-local (`review-ledger.toml`, `optimise-findings.toml`) or flow-less (`.claude/reviews/<scope>.toml`, `.claude/optimise-findings/<scope>.toml`) — share the single canonical schema defined in this section. This section is embedded verbatim into `review.md`, `review-apply.md`, `optimise.md`, and `optimise-apply.md` so every command that reads or writes a ledger sees the same rules. Read this section before touching any ledger read/write logic.
99	
100	### Canonical Ledger Schema (single source of truth)
101	
102	Both `review-ledger.toml` and `optimise-findings.toml` share this schema. Required fields marked — others optional. No inline comments in emitted TOML.
103	
104	```toml
105	schema_version = 1
106	last_updated = 2026-04-16
107	
108	[[items]]
109	id = "R1"
110	file = "src/accounting/postings.rs"
111	line = 66
112	severity = "critical"
113	effort = "small"
114	category = "quality"
115	summary = "Trade sell wrong journal entries"
116	first_flagged = 2026-04-08
117	rounds = 1
118	status = "fixed"
119	resolved = 2026-04-08
120	resolution = "Gated with BooksError in ca44570"
121	flow = "warm-meandering-zebra"
122	
123	[[items]]
124	id = "R22"
125	file = "src/events/listeners.rs"
126	line = 84
127	symbol = "listeners::trigger"
128	severity = "suggestion"
129	effort = "small"
130	category = "architecture"
131	summary = "Listeners bypass pipeline API, call deriver directly"
132	description = "Re-entrancy risk: pipeline mutex could deadlock if listeners call pipeline service."
133	first_flagged = 2026-04-08
134	rounds = 1
135	status = "deferred"
136	defer_reason = "Architectural change with re-entrancy risk"
137	defer_trigger = "When pipeline mutex is replaced with a channel-based design"
138	related = []
139	```
140	
141	#### Required fields (every item)
142	
143	- `id` — `R{n}` for review items, `O{n}` for optimise items. Stable; never renumbered; monotonic per-ledger.
144	- `file` — repo-relative file path.
145	- `line` — integer. Use `0` if no specific line applies.
146	- `severity` — `critical` | `warning` | `suggestion`.
147	- `effort` — `trivial` | `small` | `medium`.
148	- `category` — see vocabulary below.
149	- `summary` — one-line description.
150	- `first_flagged` — TOML date, ISO 8601.
151	- `rounds` — integer, incremented each time the same issue is re-flagged in a later run.
152	- `status` — see disposition vocabulary below.
153	
154	#### Optional fields
155	
156	- `symbol` — function / struct / trait method name. **Strongly recommended** for line-drift resilience; omit if no natural anchor applies.
157	- `description` — longer explanation when `summary` is insufficient.
158	- `evidence` — array of strings: doc URLs, Context7 query citations, benchmark links.
159	- `related` — array of peer IDs (e.g. `["R5", "R8"]`).
160	- `flow` — slug of the flow that contains or resolved this item. Empty/omitted for flow-less ledgers.
161	- `depends_on` — array of ledger IDs (e.g. `["O7", "R12"]`) this item must apply AFTER. Consumed by the topological sort in `/review-apply` and `/optimise-apply` Step 3. Forward references to non-existent IDs are harmless — the topo sort restricts the DAG to the selected set — but `tomlctl items orphans <ledger>` surfaces dangling refs for hygiene (emits `{"id":...,"class":"dangling-dep","dangling_deps":[...]}` records alongside `missing-file` and `symbol-missing` classes).
162	- `fingerprint` — opaque string computed by `tomlctl` (not hand-authored). Produced by `tomlctl items find-duplicates --tier B` as a 16-char SHA-256 truncation over `file|summary|severity|category|symbol`; current ledgers leave this field absent. Consumers treat absence as "fingerprint not yet computed".
163	- `rollback_rationale` — string; present on items whose transition was reverted by a Step 5.5 rollback in `/review-apply` or `/optimise-apply`. Set when a rollback flips an item from `fixed`/`applied` back to `open`. Preserved across subsequent rounds so the rollback history surfaces in future reports.
164	- `reopen_rationale` — string; present on items whose status was transitioned from `deferred` back to `open` via the deferred-trigger reopen sweep (`/review` and `/optimise` Step 1). Captures the trigger event that fired.
165	
166	#### Disposition-specific fields (required only when status matches)
167	
168	- `status = "fixed"` / `status = "applied"`:
169	  - `resolved` (date, required)
170	  - `resolution` (string, required) — commit SHA + short description.
171	- `status = "deferred"`:
172	  - `defer_reason` (string, required)
173	  - `defer_trigger` (string, required) — concrete re-evaluation condition.
174	- `status = "wontfix"` / `status = "wontapply"`:
175	  - `wontfix_rationale` (string, required).
176	- `status = "verified-clean"`:
177	  - `verified_note` (string, required) — the audit note (e.g. "Round 2 (2026-04-14) — migrations.rs idioms already match").
178	
179	#### Category vocabularies
180	
181	- **Review** (`review-ledger.toml`): `quality` | `security` | `architecture` | `completeness` | `db` | `verified-clean` (reserved for items with `status = "verified-clean"`).
182	- **Optimise** (`optimise-findings.toml`): `memory` | `serialization` | `query` | `algorithm` | `concurrency`.
183	
184	**Unknown-value fail-soft rules** (mandatory):
185	- Unknown `status` → treat as `open`.
186	- Unknown `category` → treat as `quality` (review) or `memory` (optimise); write a one-line warning to the command's console output but do not error.
187	
188	#### Disposition vocabulary
189	
190	- `open` — active, needs resolution.
191	- `deferred` — not acting now, with a concrete re-eval trigger.
192	- `fixed` (review) / `applied` (optimise) — resolved with commit evidence.
193	- `wontfix` (review) / `wontapply` (optimise) — intentional non-action with rationale.
194	- `verified-clean` (review only) — explicitly audited and confirmed clean; kept to avoid re-flagging via dedup.
195	
196	#### Render-to-markdown contract
197	
198	Commands emit TOML as the authoritative artifact. For human-readable console output, commands render items as grouped markdown tables (severity-grouped for new-finding reports; disposition-grouped for full ledger views) inline in their response. The rendered markdown is not persisted.
199	
200	#### Rollback event log
201	
202	When `/review-apply` or `/optimise-apply` Step 5.5 reverts a batch of transitions, the protocol appends one `[[rollback_events]]` table to the ledger root:
203	
204	```toml
205	[[rollback_events]]
206	timestamp = 2026-04-17T14:32:00Z
207	command = "review-apply"
208	cause = "build failure on src/accounting/postings.rs:122"
209	items = ["R3", "R7"]
210	stash_ref = "stash@{0}"
211	```
212	
213	Fields:
214	- `timestamp` — ISO 8601 date-time (seconds precision).
215	- `command` — `"review-apply"` or `"optimise-apply"`.
216	- `cause` — short description (build fail, test regression, or claimed-applied-without-diff).
217	- `items` — array of ledger IDs that were reverted back to `status = "open"`.
218	- `stash_ref` — `git stash` reference for the rolled-back working-tree state so the user can recover the changes if desired.
219	
220	`[[rollback_events]]` is append-only; existing entries are never rewritten or deleted. If the log grows unwieldy, older entries may be archived manually by moving them to `<ledger>.rollback-history.toml`; no command automates this yet.
221	
222	### Ledger TOML read/write contract
223	
224	Applies to every read/write of `review-ledger.toml` and `optimise-findings.toml`. This contract is DIFFERENT from the `context.toml` contract (single-object file, line-edit-safe) because ledgers use arrays-of-tables which are fragile under line-based editing (two items with identical `status = "open"` / `rounds = 1` lines defeat the Edit tool uniqueness).
225	
226	#### Read rules
227	
228	- **Missing `schema_version`**: treat as `1` and write it back on the next write. This is the only silent-default allowed.
229	- **`schema_version > 1`**: halt and ask the user — we don't know this format.
230	- **Missing required item field**: flag the item in the console output as malformed, skip it for resolution / dedup; do NOT attempt auto-repair.
231	- **TOML parse error**: report the error location; do NOT attempt auto-repair; ask the user to fix or restore from backup.
232	
233	#### Write strategy (MANDATORY)
234	
235	**Ledger writes MUST use parse-rewrite, not line-edit.** Preferred path — `tomlctl` (see skill `tomlctl`):
236	
237	- `tomlctl items add <ledger> --json '{...}'` — append a new item.
238	- `tomlctl items update <ledger> <id> --json '{...}'` — patch fields on an existing item matched by `id`.
239	- `tomlctl items remove <ledger> <id>` — delete by id.
240	- `tomlctl items apply <ledger> --ops '[{"op":"add|update|remove", ...}, ...]'` — batch multiple ops in one atomic, all-or-nothing file rewrite. Use this whenever touching several items in the same run so the ledger pays one parse + one write instead of N.
241	- `tomlctl set <ledger> last_updated <YYYY-MM-DD>` — bump the file-level `last_updated`.
242	- `tomlctl items next-id <ledger> --prefix R|O` — compute the next monotonic id.
243	- **Stdin for `--ops` / `--json`**: every JSON-accepting flag above treats `-` as a sentinel meaning "read JSON from stdin" — e.g. `printf '%s' "$OPS" | tomlctl items apply <ledger> --ops -`. Prefer this for large batches or payloads containing shell metacharacters (embedded quotes, `$`, backticks, or newlines in agent-produced `resolution` / `wontfix_rationale` / `verified_note` strings); avoids the tempfile round-trip and eliminates the argv-level quoting surface entirely. Empty stdin errors clearly.
244	
245	`tomlctl` writes go through `tempfile::NamedTempFile::persist` (atomic rename) and hold an exclusive advisory lock on a sidecar `.lock` file, so concurrent invocations are safe and an interrupted write cannot corrupt the ledger.
246	
247	**Fallback if `tomlctl` is unavailable** (missing binary, Rust not installed):
248	
249	1. Read the whole ledger file.
250	2. Parse it with `python3 -c "import tomllib; tomllib.load(open(PATH, 'rb'))"` (or an equivalent runtime — `python3` is assumed present on Linux; check CLAUDE.md `Build & test` section for alternatives if not).
251	3. Mutate the parsed structure in memory (add an item, change a status, increment `rounds`, etc.).
252	4. Serialise the whole structure back to TOML (preserve key order within each item per the convention below).
253	5. `Write` the new TOML over the old file in a single call.
254	
255	**Last-resort fallback** (python3 also unavailable, and the change is a single trivial edit):
256	- Read → use `Edit` with a unique surrounding context (include the preceding `id = "R{n}"` line in the match pattern to ensure uniqueness within the file).
257	- If `Edit` fails due to ambiguity: escalate to one of the parse-rewrite paths rather than approximating the match.
258	
259	#### Key-order convention (for serialisers that don't preserve order)
260	
261	When re-serialising an item, emit keys in this order:
262	`id, file, line, symbol, severity, effort, category, summary, description, evidence, first_flagged, rounds, related, status, <disposition-specific fields>, flow`
263	
264	The file-level keys come first: `schema_version`, `last_updated`, then `[[items]]` entries. `schema_version` MUST be preserved on every write.
265	
266	### Item-ID assignment and dedup
267	
268	- **ID assignment**: R-numbers for review items, O-numbers for optimise items. New items get `max(existing) + 1`. Never renumber. IDs retired by deletion are never reused.
269	- **Dedup rule (same for new-item merge AND regression detection)**: two findings match iff they have the **same `file`** AND (**same non-empty `symbol`** OR **exact `summary` string match**). No fuzzy matching, no keyword clustering. When in doubt, new ID.
270	- **Merge behaviour**:
271	  - New finding matches an `open` item → reuse the existing ID; increment `rounds`; update `last_updated` of the ledger.
272	  - New finding matches a `fixed` / `applied` item → **regression**; assign a new ID; write `related = ["<old id>"]`; flag prominently in the console report.
273	  - New finding matches a `deferred` / `wontfix` / `wontapply` / `verified-clean` item → treat as existing (no change); do not emit a new item; do not increment `rounds`. Note in console: "this matches an existing <status> item, not re-reporting."
274	- **Chronic-item escalation**: `rounds >= 3` on `open` items escalates in the summary output.
